meta.ruleset: AD&D 2nd Edition (Player's Handbook / Dungeon Master's Guide). NOT 5th edition.
meta.provenance: currency comes from PHB Table 42 and startingFunds from PHB Table 43, and equipment from PHB Table 44 (images supplied by owner). armour cost and weight come from the PHB armour table (image supplied by owner); weapons and missile ranges come from the PHB weapons table and Table 45 (images supplied by owner). Armour Class values come from PHB Table 46 (image supplied by owner). Weapons were then merged with the owner's weapons spreadsheet (hand-held and missile tabs).

sectionStatus.armour: cost, weight and Armour Class done (Table 46); movement and shield details still needed
sectionStatus.equipment: from-PHB-table-44 (weights only for tack and miscellaneous items)

openIssues: Monk house rule: monks retain no more than 25 gp per level (see house.json monk.prefill.coinLimitPerLevelGp).

Starting funds: set by the owner (dice in startingFunds.byGroup, multi-class averaged). Multi-class rounding of fractional gp is assumed up, to confirm. Override is gp-only unless you want coin mixes.
Equipment weights: clothing, food/lodging, provisioning, transport, animals and services have no weights on Table 44. Add weights if you want them in encumbrance.
Armour: movement effects, shield details and the 'Armor *' footnote were not supplied.
Weapons: Table 45 'Hammer' is the missile entry Warhammer (Thrown) (id warhammerThrown). Weapon proficiency groups / related weapons for newly added weapons are not defined yet.
Armour: elven chain (named in the thief text) is still not in the armour table. The lasso is now in weapons (from the spreadsheet).

currency.source: PHB Table 42: Standard Exchange Rates (image supplied by owner)

exchangeMatrix.meaning: matrix[row][column] = how many of the column coin one row coin is worth. E.g. matrix.gp.sp = 10 (1 gp = 10 sp); matrix.sp.gp = 1/10.

coinWeight.rule: All coin types weigh the same: 50 coins = 1 lb.

currency.crossCheck: The Rates line printed on every Tradestands sheet (1PP = 5GP = 10EP = 50SP = 500CP) matches Table 42 exactly.

weapons.source: PHB weapons table and PHB Table 45 (images supplied by owner), then updated from the owner's weapons spreadsheet (tabs 'Hand Held Weapons' and 'Missile Weapons'), which also adds non-PHB weapons and the Source, armour adjustment, racial and point-blank columns.

typeKey.note: Confirmed by owner. Combined types such as P/S mean the weapon can make either kind of attack. The type matters for the optional Weapon Type vs. Armor rule (PHB chapter 9).

footnotes.1: Inflicts double damage against charging creatures of Large or greater size.
footnotes.2: Can dismount a rider on a successful hit.
footnotes.4: Inflicts double damage when used from the back of a charging mount.
footnotes.5: Inflicts double damage when firmly set to receive a charge.
footnotes.6: Type column: Bludgeoning (B), Piercing (P), Slashing (S). Affects effectiveness against different armour types (optional rule).

weightMarkers.*: Weighs little individually. Ten of these weigh one pound. Stored as weightLbs 0.1.

fields.kind: weapon (melee or thrown), launcher (bows, crossbows, sling, blowgun) or ammunition
fields.parent: Heading the item is listed under on the table (Bow, Crossbow, Lance, Polearm, Sling, Sword, Blowgun)
fields.cost: null where the table prints a dash. 'unit' is set where the price covers several (arrows: per 12 / per 6).
fields.speedFactor: null for ammunition and for the Bastard sword (see its modes)
fields.damageSM / damageL: Small-Medium and Large damage as printed (e.g. '1d8', '1d6+1', '1d3-1'); null where the table prints a dash
fields.source: Where the weapon comes from (e.g. PHB, DMGR3, Dra #189, OA), recorded as printed in the owner's weapons spreadsheet for reference only. Weapons not on the spreadsheet keep PHB (from the PHB table). Null where the spreadsheet cell is blank.
fields.armourAdjustments: Weapon vs target Armour Class adjustment, keys '10' to '0' (spreadsheet columns 10-0). Melee/hand-held values are on the weapon (or on each mode); thrown/missile values are on the missileRanges row. Number to hit for a target AC = THAC0 - AC - adjustment (see house.json houseRules weaponVsArmourClassToHit). AC below 0 has no column.
fields.missileRanges.rows: Each row is a weapon (plus ammunition where relevant) as on the spreadsheet: rof, rangeYards (spreadsheet ranges are in units of 10 yards, checked against PHB Table 45), damageSM/damageL for that combination, armourAdjustments, pointBlank, strengthBonusApplies, additionalSpecialisationSlots, racialAttackBonus {elf, halfling} (1 = +1 to attack rolls).
fields.usage: Where the weapon appears in the app: 'melee' (hand-held list), 'missile' (missile/thrown list), or both for weapons that can be used either way (dagger, hand axe, javelin, spear, club, knife, harpoon, melee warhammer is melee only). Melee armour adjustments are on the weapon; missile ones are on its missileRanges row.

rules: ROF is the rate of fire: how many shots the weapon can make in a round. It is independent of the character's melee attacks.
Each range band includes distances equal to or less than the figure given, so a heavy crossbow fired at a target 136 yards away uses the medium range modifier.
Attack roll modifiers for range are -2 at medium range and -5 at long range.

startingFunds.status: owner house rules: 10 gp x the dice roll (this is the only ruleset; PHB Table 43 kept as phbOriginal for reference)
startingFunds.source: Owner-supplied dice. PHB Table 43 values retained per group as phbOriginal, reference only.
startingFunds.classToGroup: Use classGroups in rules-core.json (fighter/paladin/ranger = warrior, cleric/druid = priest, wizard = wizard, thief/bard = rogue).

priestRestriction.rule: Priests may spend their initial funds only on equipment and goods. Once all purchases are made, the priest returns all but two or three of his remaining gold pieces to his superiors, because his equipment is supplied by his organisation. Priests cannot lend any of their initial funds to other characters.
priestRestriction.engineHint: After the purchase step, show a prompt to remove all but 2-3 gp for priest characters.

override.behaviour: The user can type in their own starting funds instead of rolling, e.g. to follow a DM's ruling or a house rule. Stored as 'startingFundsOverrideGp'; the rolled value is kept so the user can switch back.
suggestions: Accept any whole number of gp from 0 upward.
Show a soft note (not a block) when the amount is outside the group's rolled range.
Offer a 'roll for me' button next to the override field.
override.toConfirm: Whether to also let the user set the amount as a mix of coins (PP/GP/EP/SP/CP), or gp only.

multiClass.rule: Roll the dice for each class (using that class's group dice, 10 gp x roll), add the results, and divide by the number of classes (the average of the rolls).
multiClass.classToGroup: fighter/paladin/ranger = warrior; cleric/druid = priest; wizard/illusionist = wizard; thief/bard = rogue; monk = monk

rounding.rule: Round up to a whole gp (ceiling).

multiClass.example: Fighter/Thief: 8d4 rolls 20 (200 gp) and 4d6 rolls 14 (140 gp): (200 + 140) / 2 = 170 gp.
